section_summary: This section traces Japanese tax policy from isolated liquor and municipal taxes through emergency budget measures and the broad tax revision proposed in 1936. It includes embassy and consular reports, State Department summaries, requests for translations of tax laws, and 1938 telegrams about whether taxes earmarked for military operations in China could be imposed on American citizens under the 1911 treaty.

people.name: W. Cameron Forbes
people.role: Named on a document file note as sender of an October 1930 report

people.name: Korekiyo Takahashi
people.role: Japanese Minister of Finance and former Premier

people.name: Kuroda
people.role: Named in connection with a scandal

people.name: Machida
people.role: Japanese Minister for Commerce and Industry

people.name: Andrews
people.role: Author of an embassy despatch discussed in a State Department summary

people.name: J. E. deBecker
people.role: Author of a printed English translation of the Japanese income tax law

people.name: Mr. Green
people.role: Person mentioned in a handwritten office note; identity uncertain

subfiles.title: File note on liquor tax regulations
subfiles.about: Points to a report on proposed amendments to liquor tax regulations.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Forbes’s October 1930 report on proposed liquor tax changes.

subfiles.title: Liquor taxation in Seoul
subfiles.about: Reports possible taxation of cocktails made with imported liquor in Seoul.
subfiles.summary: Authorities considered treating the mixing of imported liquors for sale as liquor manufacture.

subfiles.title: File note on the 1934–35 budget
subfiles.about: Points to despatch 454 on the budget and possible tax increases.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Grew’s despatch on the Japanese budget.

subfiles.title: File note on financing the budget deficit
subfiles.about: Points to discussion of higher taxes or a loan to cover a deficit.
subfiles.summary: Notes that a tax increase appeared likelier than a new loan.

subfiles.title: Increased taxes during the next fiscal year
subfiles.about: Discusses alternatives to borrowing for the next fiscal year's deficit.
subfiles.summary: Finance Minister Takahashi was reportedly considering moderate tax increases, while the Army favored taxes on large incomes.

subfiles.title: File note on tax policy
subfiles.about: Points to a report on disagreement over increasing taxes.
subfiles.summary: Notes Takahashi’s hesitation and Finance Ministry officials’ support for higher taxes.

subfiles.title: Government finance: taxation, inflation and silver
subfiles.about: Reviews tax policy and related financial questions.
subfiles.summary: Takahashi counseled delaying tax increases while officials favored them to reduce the deficit. The report also discusses inflation and possible effects of U.S. silver legislation.

subfiles.title: Tokyo municipal tax on household employees
subfiles.about: Reports a new Tokyo tax on employers of household servants.
subfiles.summary: The report describes the tax’s effective dates, expected revenue, exemptions and graduated rates, and cites concern about effects on employment and wages.

subfiles.title: Digest of despatch 1037
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japan’s proposed emergency taxes and 1935–36 budget deficit.
subfiles.summary: The digest outlines a proposed tax on increased corporate profits and individual incomes, the budget deficit, typhoon relief costs, public debt and debate over further bond issues.

subfiles.title: Office note concerning travel to Japan
subfiles.about: Records a telephone inquiry about a departmental decision affecting planned travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: A caller sought a decision before fixing travel plans.

subfiles.title: Japanese Government decides to increase taxes
subfiles.about: Reports Finance Minister Fujii’s proposal for an emergency profits tax.
subfiles.summary: Fujii proposed a temporary ten percent tax on increased profits and incomes to help meet the 1935–36 deficit. The despatch describes military budget demands, Osaka typhoon relief, concern about the market for deficit bonds, and debate within the cabinet and press. It also notes possible increases in postage and diversion of railway profits to the Treasury.

subfiles.title: Digest of despatch 1074
subfiles.about: Summarizes approval of the emergency tax, the budget and Fujii’s resignation.
subfiles.summary: Highlights the record defense allocation and Takahashi’s appointment as Finance Minister.

subfiles.title: Emergency tax plan, 1935–36 budget and Finance Ministry changes
subfiles.about: Reports cabinet approval of Fujii’s tax plan and details the defense budget and ministerial succession.
subfiles.summary: The cabinet approved the emergency profits tax and a ¥2.21 billion budget with ¥1.019 billion for the armed services. The despatch traces negotiations over military allocations and opposition to Fujii’s plans. Fujii resigned citing ill health, and Takahashi succeeded him and said he would maintain the settled budget.

subfiles.title: File note on emergency profits tax
subfiles.about: Points to a report on cabinet approval of Fujii’s emergency profits tax.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Grew’s despatch 1090.

subfiles.title: Cabinet approval of emergency tax
subfiles.about: Notes cabinet approval and estimated proceeds of the emergency profits tax.
subfiles.summary: Projected receipts were ¥30 million in the first year and ¥40 million thereafter.

subfiles.title: File note on business tax imposed on foreign firms
subfiles.about: Points to a letter concerning Japanese business taxes on foreign firms.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references a Chicago firm's letter about Japanese business tax.

subfiles.title: File note on Finance Ministry tax increase plan
subfiles.about: Points to a political report on the Finance Ministry’s tax increase plan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references despatch 1991.

subfiles.title: Opposition to tax increases
subfiles.about: Describes a proposed tax increase and opposition from military and commercial interests.
subfiles.summary: The plan projected ¥343.5 million in annual revenue; War Minister Terauchi preferred bond issues.

subfiles.title: Digest of Finance Minister Baba’s tax revision plan
subfiles.about: Summarizes proposed changes to direct and indirect taxes and local finance.
subfiles.summary: The digest describes higher income, inheritance, liquor and other taxes, increased central control of tax revenue, and business opposition.

subfiles.title: Finance Minister’s tax revision plan
subfiles.about: Details Baba’s proposed restructuring of Japanese taxation.
subfiles.summary: The despatch lists proposed changes to income, land, business, inheritance, liquor, excise, property, sales and other taxes. It explains the stated aims of spreading the burden more evenly, strengthening national revenue and centralizing tax authority. Business groups and newspapers disputed whether the plan would relieve rural taxpayers or instead burden consumers and industry.

subfiles.title: Finance Minister’s tax revision plan, duplicate copy
subfiles.about: Provides another copy of despatch 2063 on Baba’s tax plan.
subfiles.summary: This copy repeats the detailed schedule of proposed taxes, the shift of taxing power toward the national government, and press and business criticism.

subfiles.title: Japan’s new tax program
subfiles.about: Summarizes the new tax program and reactions from businesses and political parties.
subfiles.summary: Garrels describes changes to existing taxes, proposed gasoline, transfer, sales and property taxes, and revisions to local taxes. He reports widespread opposition and quotes the Finance Minister linking the need for lasting revenue to expected growth in military spending.

subfiles.title: Digest of despatch 2088
subfiles.about: Summarizes press criticism of Baba’s tax revision proposal.
subfiles.summary: Critics said indirect taxes and a lower income threshold would burden poorer households.

subfiles.title: Finance Minister’s project for tax revision
subfiles.about: Reports criticism of the proposed taxes and their relation to defense spending.
subfiles.summary: Baba described the plan as a response to quasi-wartime conditions. Critics argued that indirect taxes and a lower income-tax exemption would hurt ordinary people; the despatch concludes that some increase was likely because of military demands.

subfiles.title: Translation of Japanese tax laws
subfiles.about: Reports a forthcoming book of translated Japanese tax laws.
subfiles.summary: Grew offers to buy the five-yen volume for the Treasury Department if authorized.

subfiles.title: Offer of tax law publication to Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards news of the translated tax law book and offers to purchase copies.
subfiles.summary: Treasury is asked whether it wants copies at five yen each.

subfiles.title: Treasury request for Japanese tax law translations
subfiles.about: Requests complete translations of four Japanese tax laws.
subfiles.summary: Seeks income, business profits, capital interest and succession tax laws for a study of foreign taxation.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Treasury translation request
subfiles.about: Confirms that the embassy has been asked to obtain the translations.
subfiles.summary: Promises a further reply when the embassy responds.

subfiles.title: Instruction to obtain tax law translations
subfiles.about: Directs the embassy to obtain and transmit the requested tax law translations.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Treasury’s June 17 request.

subfiles.title: File note on North China tax increases
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram on temporary taxes for operations in North China.
subfiles.summary: Notes a one-year increase expected to raise ¥102 million.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Tokyo telegram excerpt
subfiles.about: Sends an excerpt about increases in Japanese taxes.
subfiles.summary: Transmits six copies of an excerpt from Grew’s August 3 telegram.

subfiles.title: Law translations for Treasury
subfiles.about: Transmits four requested English translations of Japanese tax laws.
subfiles.summary: Grew lists the income, business profits, capital interest and succession tax translations and reports their purchase cost.

subfiles.title: Forwarding translations to Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards the embassy’s despatch and four Japanese tax law translations.
subfiles.summary: Completes Treasury’s June request for translations.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about wartime taxes on Americans
subfiles.about: Asks whether Americans owe special taxes financing hostilities in China.
subfiles.summary: Requests a telegraphic interpretation of Article I of the 1911 treaty.

subfiles.title: Treaty view on military taxes
subfiles.about: States that Americans appear exempt from taxes imposed solely for hostilities in China.
subfiles.summary: Requests facts about attempted collections and advice on making representations.

subfiles.title: 1911 treaty, Article I excerpt
subfiles.about: Quotes the treaty exemption from military service and exactions.
subfiles.summary: Includes exemption from forced loans and military contributions.

subfiles.title: 1911 treaty, Article I excerpt, second copy
subfiles.about: Repeats the Article I exemption.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of the military service and exactions clause.

subfiles.title: Embassy proposal on special military taxes
subfiles.about: Proposes representations against imposing China war taxes on American citizens.
subfiles.summary: Grew explains that the taxes were assigned to special accounts for military operations and that some Americans had been asked to pay. He recommends invoking Article I of the 1911 treaty and seeking Japanese assurance that collection from Americans will cease.

subfiles.title: Approval of proposed representations
subfiles.about: Approves the embassy’s proposed action and aide-mémoire.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes the proposed approach to the Japanese Foreign Office.

subfiles.title: Japanese Foreign Office reply on special taxes
subfiles.about: Begins transmitting Japan’s reply on wartime taxes applied to Americans.
subfiles.summary: The telegram starts quoting a March 5 Foreign Office note; its text continues beyond this section.
